prompts.label: VPC ADDRESSING MODEL
prompts.placeholder: What does a subnet represent?

reveal.text: A VPC has one or more CIDR blocks. A subnet is a non-overlapping CIDR range inside the VPC and belongs to one Availability Zone. Routing and network controls then determine how resources in that subnet communicate.

prompts.label: PUBLIC OR PRIVATE IS ABOUT ROUTING
prompts.placeholder: Reveal each requirement.

cells.private: No direct default route to an internet gateway

cells.public: May be used for direct internet reachability when routing/security allow

cells.property: Outbound IPv4 internet from private resources
cells.public: Direct via IGW for appropriately addressed resources
cells.private: Commonly via NAT in a public subnet

prompts.label: LONGEST PREFIX MATCH
prompts.placeholder: How does a route table pick a route?

reveal.text: Route tables use the most specific matching destination route. A local route handles VPC-internal traffic, while other routes can point to internet gateways, NAT gateways, transit gateways, peering, endpoints, and other supported targets.

prompts.placeholder: Reveal the role of each example route.

cells.order: All applicable rules are evaluated together.

cells.why: CloudFront can offload origin traffic and improve delivery.

prompts.label: WHY ALIAS RECORDS MATTER
prompts.placeholder: What AWS-specific capability do alias records add?

reveal.text: Alias records can route Route 53 names to supported AWS resources, often including zone-apex support and AWS-aware target behavior such as Evaluate Target Health where supported.

cells.fit: On-premises systems need to resolve private AWS/VPC DNS names.

cells.selection: Lowest measured AWS network latency among configured Regions

cells.use: Shift traffic among geographically distributed resources.

prompts.label: WHAT DOES DNS QUERY LOGGING SHOW?
prompts.placeholder: What evidence does it provide?

reveal.text: DNS query logging records information about DNS queries handled by the configured Route 53 logging feature, helping operators investigate query patterns and name-resolution behavior.

Do source and return paths have the correct route targets?
Do stateful rules allow the intended traffic?
Do stateless subnet rules allow both directions/ephemeral traffic as needed?
Is something actually listening and healthy on the destination port/path?

prompts.label: WHAT DOES A FLOW LOG TELL YOU?
prompts.placeholder: Does it show packet payloads?

reveal.text: VPC Flow Logs record network-flow metadata such as addresses, ports, protocol, bytes/packets, and accept/reject decisions for supported network interfaces/resources. They do not capture application payload content.

prompts.label: INSPECT A FLOW LOG RECORD
prompts.placeholder: Click the important fields in this example flow record.

annotations.title: Source address
annotations.explanation: The source IP identifies where the flow originated.

annotations.title: Destination address
annotations.explanation: The destination IP identifies where the flow was headed.

annotations.title: Destination port
annotations.explanation: Port 443 indicates the destination service port in this record.

annotations.title: Flow action
annotations.explanation: ACCEPT means the captured flow was allowed by the applicable VPC networking controls represented by the log action field.

annotations.title: Log status
annotations.explanation: OK indicates the flow-log record was logged normally rather than being skipped because of an internal logging condition.

prompts.label: WHY IS CONTENT STALE?
prompts.placeholder: Reveal one likely cause at a time.

cells.check: Cache policy / response cache-control / object age
cells.fix: Wait for expiry or invalidate/version the object when appropriate.

cells.cause: Cache key omits a value that changes the response
cells.fix: Include the required header/cookie/query string in the cache key.

prompts.placeholder: Reveal one service at a time.

cells.fit: You need workload network-flow performance visibility.

cells.observes: Internet path and end-user network performance
cells.fit: You need visibility into internet performance affecting application users.

cells.observes: Active synthetic probes across configured network paths
cells.fit: You want proactive repeatable network tests rather than waiting for real traffic.

prompts.label: DON'T CONFUSE MONITORING WITH FLOW LOGS
prompts.placeholder: What is the distinction?

reveal.text: VPC Flow Logs are flow metadata records useful for accept/reject and traffic analysis; the CloudWatch network monitoring services focus on performance/health visibility and, for synthetic monitoring, generated probes.
